transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling really worn out almost every day. Even when I get a full night’s sleep, I wake up feeling like my body and my head are still dragging, and then I have to get through my cashier shift like that.
Do you find that you have less energy than usual or feel fatigued even after resting?
Yeah, pretty much. I feel worn out most days, even if I’ve slept through the night. When I get up for my cashier shift, my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging.
Have you noticed that you take less pleasure in things or aren’t as interested in activities you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change like that. I still do the things I usually do, maybe I’m just tired while doing them.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, more days than not?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get tired and kind of worn down, but I wouldn’t say I feel depressed most of the day. At least, I haven’t really noticed that.
Do you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or do you sleep much more than usual even though you still feel tired?

Yeah, I do. Most nights I’m tired when I get into bed, but then my mind starts going over bills, my work schedule, whether everyone at home is okay… stuff like that. I’ll eventually sleep, but I still wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
Have you noticed a decreased interest or pleasure in most activities, even the ones you used to enjoy, and how long has that been happening?

I’m not sure I’d say that’s been happening. I haven’t really noticed losing interest in most things or not enjoying them anymore. If anything, I’m just tired sometimes, but I still do the usual stuff.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus or concentrate, like trouble staying on task or making decisions?

Yeah, sometimes. At work, I can be standing at the register looking right at the screen, but my mind’s on stuff at home or bills, and I lose track. Then I have to recount the drawer or catch some little mistake I made.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively sleepy during the day, even after what you think is enough sleep at night?

Yeah, I do feel worn out during the day a lot. Even if I think I got a full night’s sleep, I’ll get up and my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging, especially when I’m getting ready for my cashier shift.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?
I don’t think so. My appetite’s been about the same, and I haven’t noticed losing weight without trying.
Do you often wake up during the night or have trouble staying asleep, or do you just feel like your sleep isn’t restful even if you don’t wake up much?

Most nights I get into bed tired, but I don’t really settle. I’ll lie there thinking about bills, my work schedule, whether everything’s okay at home. I may sleep, but it doesn’t feel restful, like I wake up feeling like I never really shut off.
How often do you have trouble settling down to sleep or feel like your sleep isn't restful — is this happening at least three nights a week, and has it been going on for a month or more?

Yeah, it’s most nights, honestly. I get into bed tired, but then I’m lying there thinking about bills, my work schedule, and if everyone at home is okay. Even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
Do you feel like your sleep is non-restorative, meaning you wake up still feeling as tired as when you went to bed, even if you didn’t wake up during the night?

Yeah, that’s pretty much it. Even if I don’t remember waking up a lot, I get up feeling like I never really settled down. I go to bed tired, but my mind keeps going over bills and work and stuff at home, so the sleep doesn’t feel like it helped much.
Can you describe how your tiredness affects your ability to get through the day, especially even after you feel like you've had enough rest?

Yeah, I feel worn out almost every day. Even if I think I slept enough, when I get up my body and my head are still dragging. By the time I’m getting ready for my cashier shift, I already feel like I’m pushing through the day instead of starting fresh.
Would you say that your lack of energy or fatigue is present most days, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yes, most days. Even when I haven’t really done much, I still feel worn out. I can get a full night’s sleep and still wake up with my body and my head dragging, like I’m already tired before I even get to my cashier shift.
Do you find it hard to think clearly or concentrate on tasks, even simple ones, because your mind feels tired or overwhelmed?

Yeah, I do. Even with simple stuff at the register, I can be looking right at the screen and still kind of lose track because I’m thinking about bills or things at home. Then I’ll have to recount the drawer or catch some small mistake I made.
Would you say that your fatigue and unrefreshing sleep happen even when your mood is relatively stable and you’re not particularly stressed or down?

Yeah, even when I’m not especially upset or anything, I still feel worn out. I can get what seems like a full night’s sleep, but when I get up for my cashier shift, my body and my head are still dragging.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or lost interest in things for several days at a time, even when you’re not particularly tired?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I have off days like anyone, but I haven’t noticed feeling down or losing interest for several days in a row like that.
Over the past two weeks, have you found yourself losing interest in things or not getting as much pleasure out of activities, even when you’re not particularly tired?
I don’t think so, not really. I mean, if I don’t do something it’s usually because I’m tired or distracted, but I haven’t noticed that I just don’t enjoy things anymore.
Have you noticed yourself having trouble getting started on tasks or feeling like everything takes extra effort, even when you’re not necessarily feeling down or stressed?

Yeah, I do feel like that sometimes. It’s mostly like I’m just worn out almost every day. Even if I got a full night’s sleep, when I get up for my cashier shift my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging, so getting going takes more effort than it should.
